result:
Post revisions are implemented. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (11 tests, 9 of them new), and the full `bunx guren gate` passes too. Nothing is committed; the changes are in the working tree.

One behaviour to be aware of: a save that changes nothing still keeps a revision. I took "every successful edit keeps the previous version" literally; say so if you'd rather skip no-op saves.

## Summary

I added a `post_revisions` table (`id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` as ISO text) to `db/schema.ts`, with a generated migration in `db/migrations/20260929165131_add_post_revisions/`, plus a `PostRevision` model in `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`. `app/Models/Post.ts` gained `Post.revise()`, which snapshots the current version and applies the new content in one transaction, and `Post.destroyWithRevisions()`, which deletes a post's revisions with the post; `PostController.update` and `destroy` now call these. The new `app/Http/Controllers/PostRevisionController.ts` serves `GET /posts/:id/revisions` (props `post` and `revisions`, newest first) and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` (redirects to `/posts/:id`, 404 for a revision of a different post), both registered in the auth group in `routes/web.ts` so guests go to `/login`. Non-authors get 403 through a new `manageRevisions` ability in `app/Policies/PostPolicy.ts`. Supporting pieces are `PostRevisionResource`, `PostRevisionParamSchema` in `PostValidator.ts`, the page `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`, a "Revisions" link for the author in `posts/Show.tsx`, and the regenerated `.guren/*.gen.ts` files. The feature tests are in `tests/PostRevisionController.test.ts` and run against the test database.
